hook.text: Smoked salmon gets its flavor from over 200 chemical compounds deposited by wood smoke. No two woods taste alike.

buildup.text: Wood smoke contains phenols, carbonyls, and organic acids that penetrate food surfaces and add flavor.

discovery.text: Phenols from smoke also act as antioxidants and antimicrobials—smoking preserves food while flavoring it.

twist.text: Liquid smoke is real smoke condensed into liquid—same compounds, no fire needed. Chemically identical flavor.

climax.text: Hickory gives bacon its classic taste. Applewood adds sweetness. Mesquite delivers intensity. Wood choice is everything.

punchline.text: Smoke is flavor, preservative, and color in one chemical package.

quiz.question: What is liquid smoke?
options: Real wood smoke condensed into liquid form—same compounds
